literature_notes: The sole ledger line (L1) describes the 'L-gp130' chimeric construct (PMC11526557), in which wild-type IL6ST is truncated ~15 residues above the TM domain (around residue 603, computed as 618−15) and the entire native extracellular domain is replaced by the leucine zipper of human c-JUN fused to a FLAG tag. The FLAG tag therefore resides in the heterologous c-JUN leucine zipper sequence, not in any native IL6ST residue. This is a chimeric receptor analogous to a CAR construct: the native ectodomain is absent, so no junction in the native IL6ST extracellular span (residues 23–617) can be inferred. The construct is membrane-anchored and the FLAG is extracellular, but the tag cannot be mapped to an insert_after_residue in the canonical IL6ST sequence. None of the disqualifying categories (soluble ectodomain, Fc-fusion, antibody epitope mapping, commercial plasmid with unstated position, intracellular tag) apply, but the fundamental requirement — that the tag be inserted into the native protein sequence at a pinnable position — is not met. Accordingly, zero sites are reported.
